fullPassage: The expression "Moveable Feast" originally referred to the changing date of religious celebrations. It was later adopted by Ernest Hemingway to describe his experience of living in Paris. We use the term Moveable Feast to conceptualize the potentiality to connect with people, ideas, and information at any time and in any place. In the Digital Age, information circulates and travels not only in a straight line from official media outlets to consumers but has the potential to move from anyone to everyone else. The Moveable Feast is a table filled with information "dishes" that have been prepared by participating members of the feast. Each person may try a slice of everyone else's dish. Furthermore, this feast moves around the entire world and interacts with billions of other feasts-of-digits, complete with servings of information that are monitored by platforms and governments. At any given point in time, each person has the potential to connect with any other person by sampling their information, and perhaps by "dishing dirt" of their own, or by rejecting dishes that are not particularly tasty. This feast features all the components of social interaction in complex, dynamic information environments; as Hemingway most aptly described, "it stays with you" wherever you go.

questions.passage: The expression "Moveable Feast" originally referred to the changing date of religious celebrations. It was later adopted by Ernest Hemingway to describe his experience of living in Paris. We use the term Moveable Feast to conceptualize the potentiality to connect with people, ideas, and information at any time and in any place. In the Digital Age, information circulates and travels not only in a straight line from official media outlets to consumers but has the potential to move from anyone to everyone else. The Moveable Feast is a table filled with information "dishes" that have been prepared by participating members of the feast. Each person may try a slice of everyone else's dish. Furthermore, this feast moves around the entire world and interacts with billions of other feasts-of-digits, complete with servings of information that are monitored by platforms and governments. At any given point in time, each person has the potential to connect with any other person by sampling their information, and perhaps by "dishing dirt" of their own, or by <u>rejecting</u> dishes that are not particularly tasty. This feast features all the components of social interaction in complex, dynamic information environments; as Hemingway most aptly described, "it stays with you" wherever you go.

❌ ④ removing — 제거하기 (의미축 다름: 삭제)
det.tip: rejecting(거부하기) ↔ accepting(받아들이기). refusing은 오히려 동의어이므로 함정
